archetype: Mono-green flash-ambush stompy: a 37-creature midrange deck wearing a draw-go posture. The strategic frame describes it correctly in prose, but its 'control' self-label made the audit's archetype matcher apply control overrides (37-39 lands, 12-15 removal, 5-7 wipes) that fit a wrath deck, not this one — three of the four UNDER verdicts are inflated by that override.
verdict: The mana is the best-measured in the fleet's terms (52 Burgess sources vs 36, turn-3 land hit 0.91, commander mean cast t4.0) and the ambush machinery is verified and dense (flash trap drawn 92.5%, metronome body 96.8%). What binds is still board WIDTH: the kill needs five bodies (stack 003) and the goldfish reaches a mean of 3.638 by t6, crossing the bar only around t8 (5.074), with finisher-plus-second-wave assembled 39.5% by t6. The applied swaps closed the graveyard hole (interaction-breadth 5/5) and widened the board for free; the one genuine coverage hole left is zero mass removal. Stack 005 sharpened the plan itself: the end-step Craterhoof is legal but its pump dies in that turn's cleanup — bodies deploy at end steps (006: they wake attack-ready), the finisher is an own-main cast.

axes.reading: The 37-39 band is the control-archetype override; the deck's own archetype is creature midrange, Burgess's source formula is cleared with 16 copies to spare, and the turn-3 land hit is 0.91 against a 0.74 floor. A 37th land is not the marginal use of a slot here.

axes.reading: At the floor of 10, and the count overstates uniform quality: only Beast Whisperer draws on every creature cast ungated — Garruk's Uprising gates on power 4+ (three fixed bodies: Dawn's Light Archer, Old Fat Spider, Craterhoof — Wickerbough Elder enters with a -1/-1 counter as a 3/3 and never fires it — plus Mirkwood Pathmaker whenever lands ≥4), Elemental Bond and Tribute's draw half gate on power 3+ (nine fixed bodies plus Pathmaker), Selvala needs strictly-greatest power, Frostfang and Toski need combat damage to connect, Fecundity needs deaths, and Harmonize is one-shot. GAS drawn 85.3% is drawn, not firing.

axes.reading: Now 10, and still wrong in both directions: it includes Devoted Druid, whose removal:debuff tag is a misfile (its -1/-1 counter is a cost it puts on itself — it removes nothing of an opponent's), so the real removal-class count is 9 — while the flash-trap deterrence the deck leans on stays invisible to it. The applied swaps improved exactly the weak flank: Deathgorge Scavenger answers graveyards repeatably and Hornet Queen brings the deck's first deathtouch BLOCKERS beyond Hornet Nest's tokens (Frostfang's deathtouch is still attackers-only, Saryth's tapped-only). The residual gap to the 12-15 band is the control override already adjudicated under mana-base.

cut_candidates.why: The only one-shot in a ten-card engine suite; every other draw source compounds with the board. If a slot must be found for a body, this is the card whose job the engines already do when the deck is functioning.
cut_candidates.cost_of_cutting: It is the deck's ONLY unconditional draw — no board, no combat, no deaths required — which makes it the best card in exactly the games where the deck is losing. Cutting it also drops card-advantage from 10 to 9, below the ratios floor, unless the replacement draws.

open_questions.question: How much do the goldfish's three declared blind spots (no discount, no opponent-turn flash casts, no aura ramp) understate board density?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Board width is the binding axis and its true value is unmeasured; stack 006 confirms end-step bodies fight the next turn, so the floor is real, but if true bodies-by-t6 is near 5 the deck needs nothing further, and if it is near the measured 3.638 it still wants Avenger-class width and possibly Seedborn Muse.
